name: Ji Junxiang
dates: fl. second half of the 13th century
bio: Ji Junxiang (紀君祥) was a playwright of the Yuan dynasty from Dadu (modern Beijing). The Register of Ghosts (錄鬼簿, c. 1330) lists him among the early zaju dramatists and credits him with six plays, of which only one survives complete.

That play, The Orphan of Zhao (趙氏孤兒), dramatises the revenge of the last heir of the house of Zhao on the minister who destroyed it. It was the first Chinese drama to be translated in Europe, by the Jesuit Joseph de Prémare in 1731, and inspired Voltaire's L'Orphelin de la Chine (1755).
